name: Ideal Power Inc.
thesis: Ideal Power licenses B-TRAN, the only bidirectional bipolar transistor in existence: one device that conducts and blocks in both directions, halving conduction loss versus the back-to-back MOSFET/IGBT pairs every solid-state circuit breaker uses today. Nvidia's 800VDC Rubin Ultra rack architecture creates a socket that no incumbent device fills well, and a US hyperscaler is co-developing an 800V DC prototype for exactly that architecture. Market cap $63.9m at the 2026-09-16 close with $41.3m of cash and essentially no debt, so the market values the whole platform at roughly $22m.
why_10x: 10x = $639m; since $41m of the $64m is cash, the operating business need only reach ~$598m. That requires one pathway - datacentre SSCB or EV contactor - to convert into a production design-in with device or royalty revenue in the tens of millions. An emerging power-semi platform with a named hyperscaler and a named auto OEM at $600m is unremarkable for the category. 100x = $6.4bn is arithmetically live (Navitas has traded near that on GaN) if B-TRAN becomes standard content in both DC datacentre protection and EV contactors; low probability, but the ~14-15 quarter runway is long enough to find out.
what_kills_it: Pre-revenue for over a decade with a prior pivot (it was a solar inverter company) and $5,800 of quarterly revenue; hyperscaler co-development routinely ends without a purchase order and the partner is unnamed so nothing can be independently verified; Infineon/onsemi/Wolfspeed/Navitas can attack the same sockets with proven SiC and GaN at scale, and double-sided wafer processing is a real yield risk at volume.

name: Voyager Therapeutics, Inc.
thesis: Voyager is an AAV capsid arms dealer, not a drug developer. Its TRACER platform screens capsid libraries directly in non-human primates for blood-brain-barrier crossing after ordinary IV dosing plus liver de-targeting - the actual binding constraint on CNS gene therapy, since AAV9 crosses poorly and today's therapies need neurosurgery. Fourteen partnered TRACER-enabled programmes pay milestones and royalties regardless of which disease wins. SEC-verified cash and investments of $148.8m at 30-Jun-2026 against a $187.9m market cap leaves an enterprise value near $39m.
why_10x: 10x = $1.88bn. Two or three of the 14 partnered programmes must reach late-stage development, converting contingent milestones into a visible royalty stream, plus two further large capsid deals. A royalty business with $150-250m of annual milestone-and-royalty income trades at 8-12x revenue. Critically this requires no Voyager-owned drug to work at all. 100x = $18.8bn implies Royalty Pharma-scale economics from a capsid estate - conceivable over 15 years, not a 5-10 year case.
what_kills_it: Capsid obsolescence - focused-ultrasound BBB opening, engineered exosomes or rival capsids from Capsida, Dyno or Regenxbio commoditise TRACER, and there is no regulatory moat; partner attrition, since licensees can walk and Voyager gets nothing further, with a Novartis deprioritisation removing the anchor; and burn of ~$22.9m a quarter means the cash cushion that makes the EV look cheap is being spent on an owned pipeline worth possibly less than the cash. The company has already failed twice - this is its third business model.

name: AML3D Limited
thesis: AML3D sells ARCEMY, a containerised wire-arc additive manufacturing cell that 3D-prints large metal parts from welding wire. The mechanism is a physical bottleneck in AUKUS: the US submarine industrial base cannot hit Virginia-class build rates because castings and forgings carry 18-36 month lead times and many original manufacturers no longer exist. Through BlueForge Alliance the US Navy is installing AML3D machines across its own supply chain rather than merely buying parts - six units at Newport News Shipbuilding and three at Austal USA. FY26 revenue A$12.5m (+70%) with the first EBITDA-positive half.
why_10x: 10x = US$545m from US$54.5m. That needs roughly A$90-120m of revenue at 5-7x sales - about 8-10x FY2026 - achieved by going from a handful of installed systems to 100-150 across US, UK and Australian naval supply chains plus the consumables and licence tail. At A$2-4m per system plus service, 100 systems is A$200-400m of cumulative hardware with recurring revenue underneath. This is the most mechanically checkable 10x in the sleeve: arithmetic on machine count, not a scientific breakthrough. 100x (US$5.5bn) would need WAAM to displace a large share of global castings and forgings with AML3D holding the standard - a 2-3% tail.
what_kills_it: Sovereignty risk - an Australian supplier inside a US sovereign defence programme is permanently exposed to the Navy insourcing WAAM or mandating a domestic vendor, and this is unhedgeable; qualification slippage, since additive metal has repeatedly under-delivered on timelines and the jump to safety-critical parts may never come; and contract lumpiness, where one delayed system flips the half back into loss on a A$12.5m revenue base.

name: ONWARD Medical N.V.
thesis: ONWARD develops ARC Therapy - targeted spinal cord stimulation that amplifies surviving nerve signal below a spinal cord injury to restore movement, blood pressure and autonomic function. ARC-EX is FDA-cleared and selling (159 units in H1 2026, +430% year on year, 130+ US clinics, VA home-use access); ARC-IM is the implant; ARC-BCI couples the implant to a cortical BCI so the patient's own intention drives stimulation. It is the only listed BCI pure-play - Neuralink, Precision, Paradromics and Synchron are all private - and unlike them it already has revenue and reimbursement data.
why_10x: 10x = US$2.23bn. ARC-EX must reach roughly EUR 50-80m of annual revenue with permanent reimbursement, and ARC-IM must hit its pivotal blood-pressure endpoint to give ONWARD an approved implant. An approved neuromodulation implant with a BCI roadmap would be valued like an early Inspire Medical or Axonics - both exceeded $3bn - plus the scarcity premium of being the only listed BCI pure-play. 100x (US$22bn) is not defensible: US SCI prevalence is roughly 300,000 people, and even with Parkinson's and stroke extensions the market does not support it.
what_kills_it: Dilution rather than death - EUR 24.7m lost in six months on EUR 4.2m of revenue, share count already +55.8% in 18 months, so holders can be right on the science and still lose; reimbursement is the real gate, and without a permanent CMS code ARC-EX stays a cash-pay and VA niche; and a missed Empower BP endpoint removes the implant leg entirely, leaving a thinly-traded external-device company on ~US$373k a day.

name: Lightbridge Corporation
thesis: Lightbridge develops an all-metallic, helically-twisted multi-lobe nuclear fuel rod designed as a drop-in replacement for uranium-oxide fuel in existing PWRs and SMRs. Fuel, not reactors, is where nuclear economics change fastest: a fuel letting each of roughly 440 operating reactors produce ~10% more electricity from the same steel needs no new build, site or grid connection, only NRC qualification. The striking fact is the balance sheet - $237.5m of cash, zero debt, against a $228.0m market cap at the 2026-09-16 close of $6.47, its 52-week low. Enterprise value is negative.
why_10x: 10x = $2.28bn. It requires the ATR loop campaign to produce clean irradiation data, DOE to authorise the SHED pilot facility, and at least one US utility to commit to Lead Test Assemblies in a commercial core; the market would then price Lightbridge as a fuel licensor with line of sight to single-digit share of the ~$10bn/yr global fabrication market plus uprate economics. Because enterprise value is negative the technology option is free, so on EV any successful qualification produces an unbounded multiple. On market cap, 100x ($22.8bn) would require dominating Western fleet fuel supply against Westinghouse, Framatome and GNF - implausible.
what_kills_it: The clock rather than the balance sheet - fuel qualification is a 10-15 year regulatory marathon and the ATR loop campaign alone runs about 60 months, so the thesis can time out inside a 5-10 year hold; metallic fuel physics, since metallic fuels have historically suffered swelling and fuel-cladding chemical interaction at high burn-up and there is no fallback product; and a decade-long management record of announcing pathways rather than delivering fuel, funded throughout by dilution (+87.6% shares in 21 months), against utilities that are intensely conservative about core loading.

name: Aclara Resources Inc.
thesis: Aclara is an ionic adsorption clay rare-earth developer with the Penco Module in Chile, the flagship Carina Module in Brazil, and a planned heavy rare earth separation facility in Louisiana - intended to be the first in the United States. The US has no domestic heavy rare earth separation capability at all: dysprosium and terbium, the elements that let a magnet survive motor temperatures, are almost entirely Chinese. Ionic clays are the geological prize because the heavies desorb with a mild salt solution at ambient temperature, with no crushing, roasting or thorium waste stream, and almost every such deposit sits in China or Myanmar.
why_10x: 10x = US$6.49bn from US$649m. That needs Carina in production, the Louisiana separation plant operating, and Aclara established as the West's primary non-Chinese dysprosium and terbium supplier with binding offtakes at strategic pricing. MP Materials reached a multi-billion valuation on light rare earths alone with a US price floor; a heavy rare earth equivalent with EXIM project financing and two producing modules supports the number. 100x = US$65bn exceeds the plausible value of the entire rare earth industry outside China - the arithmetic does not close.
what_kills_it: Chile - Penco was previously rejected on environmental grounds and the company relinquished all water rights in December 2025 to get it through, so community opposition can return and has before; the EXIM Letter of Interest is explicitly non-binding and many never convert, and with ~$42.6m of cash against a multi-hundred-million build a failure to convert forces heavy dilution; and rare earth prices are administered by Chinese policy, so a deliberate price war can render every Western project uneconomic mid-construction, with minorities in a 74.5%-controlled, ~US$248k-a-day stock powerless to respond.

name: Silex Systems Limited
thesis: Silex owns the SILEX laser uranium enrichment process and holds 51% of Global Laser Enrichment, a JV with Cameco (49%), building the Paducah Laser Enrichment Facility in Kentucky. Enrichment, not reactors, is the true chokepoint - every SMR, HALEU reactor and LEU+ uprate consumes SWU, and the West lost roughly 45% of supply when Russian enriched product was sanctioned. Laser separation uniquely can economically re-enrich DOE's stockpile of over 200,000 tonnes of depleted tails under a 2016 agreement running up to 30 years, feedstock incumbents cannot touch. Near-breakeven EBITDA and US$128.5m of investments make it unusually survivable for a moonshot.
why_10x: 10x = US$8.69bn. It needs PLEF licensed, built and operating at planned scale with conversion and enrichment services attached; at mid-cycle pricing that is a multi-hundred-million-dollar annual EBITDA asset, and Silex's 51% share on Centrus-type multiples supports the number. The required conditions are specific and checkable: licence granted, JV funded without Silex diluting below 51%, enrichment pricing sustained above roughly US$120/SWU. 100x = US$87bn is larger than the plausible enterprise value of the entire Western enrichment industry combined.
what_kills_it: The capital call - a GLE final investment decision forces Silex to fund 51% of a multi-billion-dollar plant, so it either issues heavy equity at a depressed price or dilutes below 51% and loses control; this is the most probable value-destroying path and it is triggered by success, not failure. Second, NRC licensing can slip or fail, and nobody outside the classified programme can independently verify that separation factors hold at full cascade scale. Third, Cameco holds half the money and the commercial channel and could walk, while a peace settlement restoring Russian enriched product would collapse SWU pricing.

name: Nyxoah SA
thesis: Nyxoah makes Genio, a bilateral hypoglossal nerve stimulator for obstructive sleep apnoea in CPAP-intolerant patients. Unlike the incumbent implant it has no battery and no lead - a chip under the chin powered externally by a nightly disposable patch - so there is no replacement surgery every 10-11 years, and it is MRI-compatible. Bilateral stimulation lets Genio treat complete concentric collapse, a population for which the incumbent device is contraindicated. This is not a market that must be created: Inspire Medical proved physicians implant these and payers reimburse them, so Nyxoah only has to take share.
why_10x: 10x = $1.58bn. Nyxoah needs roughly $250-350m of revenue - about ten times current - at 60-70% gross margins valued at 5-6x sales, implying 800-1,200 active implanting centres and 10-15% share of the US HGNS market. Inspire's own trajectory shows that revenue level is attainable in this category; the question is purely whether Nyxoah funds the commercial build without destroying the equity. 100x = $15.8bn is roughly the whole OSA neurostimulation category at maturity - possible in theory, improbable given the dilution its burn makes near-certain.
what_kills_it: The financing rather than the science - a ~$110m annual loss against ~$45m of net cash ($97.8m cash and investments less $52.6m debt) means repeated raises at a $158m market cap, and the share count is already up 172% in 18 months, so holders can be entirely right about Genio and still be diluted out of the return. Second, Inspire has a decade of physician relationships, a built salesforce and the balance sheet to compete on price while Nyxoah is capital-constrained. Third, any adverse safety finding in the BREATHE post-approval study would be fatal to a single-product company with no cash buffer.

name: Aeluma, Inc.
thesis: Aeluma grows compound-semiconductor (III-V) material directly on large-diameter silicon wafers and builds photodetectors, lasers and infrared sensors from it, targeting AI/datacentre optical interconnect, defence and aerospace sensing, mobile, automotive lidar, AR/VR and quantum. Co-packaged optics is the declared 2026-28 hyperscaler roadmap and the binding constraint is that every optical engine today imports its laser and detector as separate III-V die - Aeluma attacks exactly that bottleneck, and US industrial policy is now funding it directly. It sells development contracts and NRE today, not volume product: FY2026 revenue $4.5m, Q4 FY2026 $0.6m vs $1.3m prior year, FY2026 net loss $9.2m, gross margin 37.7%, cash $56.0m at 30 June 2026 (>3 years of runway). All seven fact-checked claims confirmed verbatim.
why_10x: 10x on the 16 September close is ~$2.1bn. Aeluma must convert CHIPS money and the Tower production-foundry flow into a qualified 200/300mm III-V-on-Si process with a named datacom or defence customer shipping volume, taking revenue from $4.5m to $100m+. At $2.1bn it would trade as a scarce US-domiciled photonics materials platform - below what compound-semiconductor substrate peers command, so the multiple is not the stretch; the revenue is. The $56m cash pile buys the three-plus years that most moonshots do not have. 100x is $21bn, roughly Coherent's position as default laser supplier: conceivable on a 15-year view, not underwriteable now.
what_kills_it: Revenue is going backwards - FY2026 fell to $4.5m and Q4 halved to $0.6m; the company is being paid to do research and even that is lumpy. The physics may not scale: defect density in III-V grown on large silicon wafers is the standing objection that has defeated far better-resourced organisations. The CHIPS letter of intent is politically contingent and explicitly non-binding, and at ~$211m on $4.5m of revenue success is already embedded in the price. Falsifying fact: FY2027 passing without a commercial (non-government) design win in datacom optics.

name: Weebit Nano Limited
thesis: Weebit Nano licenses ReRAM, a non-volatile embedded memory intended to replace embedded flash below 28nm, where flash physically stops scaling. This is a pure semiconductor-IP model: licence fees and NRE now, production royalties later, at IP margins. FY2026 revenue A$15.3m (+158% y/y), gross margin ~100%, cash A$168.3m at 30 Jun 2026 against an A$57m annual burn - funded to the royalty inflection. The validation is unusually hard for a pre-royalty IP company: Texas Instruments licensed the technology in December 2025 and is described as Weebit's largest customer to date; onsemi 65nm BCD demo chips are performing as expected; DB HiTek has JEDEC-qualified it in a 130nm BCD process across three wafer lots.
why_10x: 10x = ~A$7.3bn (~US$4.9bn). ReRAM must become the default embedded NVM below 28nm across three or more major foundries, with royalties compounding toward a few hundred million dollars a year at IP margins. That is a normal valuation for a successful semiconductor IP company - and it is among the most mechanically plausible 10x paths in the sleeve because the royalty arithmetic is already known; only the adoption rate is uncertain. 100x (~US$49bn) would put a single memory-IP family near Arm's valuation - no.
what_kills_it: Royalties keep moving right - now a 2027 story, and they have slipped before; until they arrive, revenue is NRE that stops when the work stops. The burn is A$57m a year against A$15m of revenue: the A$168m cash pile came from shareholders, not operations, and the register has been diluted heavily to build it. MRAM is the incumbent alternative (Everspin, GlobalFoundries, Samsung) with more design wins in some segments, and two tier-1 licences are already in the price. Insider ownership of 7% is the one alignment weakness.

name: Vulcan Energy Resources Limited
thesis: Vulcan Energy is building the world's first integrated geothermal-plus-direct-lithium-extraction operation in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley Brine Field, producing lithium hydroxide and district heat from the same brine. The single most important fact is the financing: a EUR 2.2bn Lionheart Phase One package closed December 2025 with EIB committing EUR 250m inside a syndicate of a dozen-plus banks and export credit agencies - a dozen sophisticated lenders have done the diligence for you, which is rare at a ~A$1bn equity value. Product already exists (geothermal heat has been flowing to Landau since April 2025); lithium production is targeted for 2028. Correction applied: the BASF permits of Feb 2025 covered 2D survey measurements only, with 3D flagged as a possible follow-on, not as already permitted.
why_10x: 10x = ~US$7.5bn (~A$10.7bn). Requires Lionheart Phase One delivered on budget at 24,000 tpa, Phase Two sanctioned, and lithium hydroxide back above ~US$20,000/t with a European green premium. Own arithmetic: at 24,000 tpa and a US$8,000/t margin Phase One alone is ~US$190m EBITDA; a 48,000 tpa business plus a 30-year geothermal annuity at 15-18x supports the target. The structural case is that Europe has no domestic lithium chemical supply and Vulcan's product is net-zero by construction. 100x (US$75bn) exceeds Albemarle and SQM at their peaks combined - not possible.
what_kills_it: First-of-a-kind commissioning risk: no integrated geothermal-DLE plant of this scale exists anywhere, and Upper Rhine geothermal carries a history of induced seismicity - Basel and Landau projects were stopped by it - so a felt earthquake is a political event, not just a technical one. Lithium prices staying depressed for years: the plant gets built and the equity still earns nothing. And the EUR 2.2bn is DEBT - at a ~A$1bn equity value the project is heavily geared, a cost overrun impairs equity first, and FCF of -A$246m shows cash already going out of the door.

name: Intellicheck, Inc.
thesis: Intellicheck does authoritative-source identity validation - it reads the encoded data on a US driver's licence and checks it against exclusive state DMV data relationships rather than inspecting an image. That contractual data access, not the software, is the moat, and it cannot be reproduced by a better-funded competitor buying GPUs. TTM revenue $24.11m (+16.7%), gross margin 91%, net income $3.14m / EPS $0.15, ~500 revenue-generating enterprise customers across banking, fintech, retail and government, no debt, positive cash flow - on a $48.0m market cap after a 57% de-rating.
why_10x: 10x = $483m. That needs revenue of roughly $70-90m - three to four times current - at the same 91% margin, with operating leverage taking net margin to 20-25%; on 6-8x sales or 25-30x earnings that clears $480m. This is the most arithmetically ordinary 10x in the sleeve: it requires no new scientific category, only a small company with an unreproducible data asset compounding at 15-25% for six or seven years while state age-verification and KYC statutes keep expanding the addressable transaction count. With only 20.3m shares out, a single large contract moves EPS visibly. 100x ($4.8bn) would need $600m-1bn of revenue and would be acquired long before.
what_kills_it: Customer concentration - a handful of large financial-services accounts drive revenue; losing one shows up immediately in a quarter, which is what a 57% drawdown on a profitable company usually means the market is already pricing. It may simply be a niche vendor: 16-17% growth is respectable, not explosive, and Socure, Persona, LexisNexis and Experian are better capitalised and can bundle identity into broader contracts. Acquisition at a modest premium caps the upside - with a $48m cap, no debt and clean cash flow, a 40% premium take-out is plausible and thesis-ending.

name: Gelion plc
thesis: Gelion is a ~GBP33m AIM lithium-sulphur battery company at 14.5p, licensing a sulphur cathode rather than building gigafactories, so it does not need heavy capital. Li-S offers a step-change in gravimetric energy density with no nickel and no cobalt, which is why the first real markets are drones and defence, where weight dominates cost. Revenue GBP2.84m (+32.8%), cash GBP10.52m, no debt, insiders 39.55%. The partner list is far better than a GBP33m AIM company normally assembles. All RNS dates confirmed verbatim against Investegate.
why_10x: 10x = ~GBP333m (US$444m). It needs one named, royalty-bearing licence with a global cell maker plus a defence or drone design win, taking licence and royalty revenue to roughly GBP15-25m annualised. On the 15-20x revenue multiple licensing models attract once the counterparty is named, GBP333m is reachable from GBP33m - the licensing model means the capital requirement to get there is modest, which is what makes the arithmetic work. 100x is US$4.4bn, requiring Li-S to displace lithium-ion in a mainstream mass market inside the holding period - not credible; cycle life is the reason.
what_kills_it: The Oxis Energy base rate - a UK Li-S company with real IP and real partners went into administration in 2021 doing exactly this; that is the honest prior. Cycle life is unsolved physics: the polysulphide shuttle has defeated forty years of attempts, and if the cathode cannot exceed a few hundred cycles it is a niche drone product. Every major commercial relationship is unnamed - the tier-one partner, the exclusive licensee and the funded scale-up counterparty are all anonymous - and with ~GBP26k of daily turnover you can neither verify the thesis nor exit it.

name: Editas Medicine, Inc.
thesis: Editas Medicine has pivoted to EDIT-401, an in vivo LNP-delivered gene editor that up-regulates LDL receptor expression in the liver, aiming to cut LDL-C, Lp(a) and ApoB simultaneously with a single dose. That is a different and more ambitious mechanism than the PCSK9-knockdown editors, and it is aimed at the largest chronic-disease market in medicine. The company holds exclusive Broad Institute / Harvard licences to foundational Cas9 and Cas12a patents, giving freedom to operate and leverage over other editors. Best-funded name in its batch, with runway extended into H2 2028 and 79.2% institutional ownership; a dated binary readout sits inside the holding period.
why_10x: 10x = $4.2bn. EDIT-401 must reproduce even half the primate lipid effect in humans with clean safety, and Editas must sign a large-pharma partner. The comparable is priced: Lilly paid roughly $1.3bn upfront plus CVRs for Verve on PCSK9 editing data alone, so a one-shot triple-lipid editor with human data should be worth several multiples of that; $4.2bn is roughly where Intellia peaked in 2021 on comparable evidence. 100x is $42bn - cardiovascular outcomes trials run to tens of thousands of patients and are far beyond this company, so the equity will almost certainly be crystallised by a takeout in the $3-8bn range.
what_kills_it: Translation failure - primate lipid effects have translated poorly before, and LDLR up-regulation may prove less durable in humans than knockdown; a Q1 2027 update showing 30% rather than 90% reduction ends it. Safety: liver off-target editing or an LNP immune response, in a PREVENTION indication where tolerance for harm is near zero. Zero insider ownership and a record of pivots - management holds 0.18%, and Editas has pivoted from LCA10 to sickle cell to lipids with each pivot destroying value. Note the H1 2026 revenue line is a one-off from the Bristol Myers Squibb opt-in EXPIRING - a relationship ending, not deepening.

name: Smart Eye AB (publ)
thesis: Smart Eye supplies driver monitoring systems and interior sensing to automotive OEMs, a category that stopped being optional: EU General Safety Regulation driver-drowsiness and attention-warning requirements became binding during 2026, making DMS a regulatory line item on new type approvals rather than a premium feature. The setup is unusually concrete for a moonshot: 379 cumulative design wins across 24 OEMs, >SEK 7.6bn of estimated remaining lifetime order value (roughly 3.6x the market cap), 20 customers already in production across 175 models, 128% automotive organic growth, EBITDA turned positive, and the stock at a 52-week low.
why_10x: 10x = ~SEK 21bn (US$2.1bn). It requires the SEK 7.6bn order book to convert plus continued win accumulation, taking revenue to roughly SEK 1.5-2bn at software gross margins with real operating profit - an ordinary valuation for a profitable automotive software supplier with that backlog. The margin kicker is Interior Sensing upsold onto existing DMS programmes: follow-on orders require no change to the software, so incremental wins drop through at near-full margin. 100x (US$21bn) is not defensible for an automotive software supplier and should not be underwritten.
what_kills_it: Net debt of ~SEK 300m against SEK 86m of cash with negative free cash flow - the company has grown revenue for years without converting it to cash, so another dilutive raise before breakeven is the live risk, and it would be priced off a 52-week low. Competition that can bundle: Seeing Machines competes directly while Bosch, Continental and Aptiv can give DMS away inside a cockpit domain controller, and Chinese OEMs increasingly use domestic DMS. Design-win value is an estimate of future deliveries, not a contracted minimum - it can be cancelled with a model programme.

name: Quantum-Si Incorporated
thesis: Semiconductor-chip single-molecule protein sequencing from the founder of 454 Life Sciences and Ion Torrent. Platinum ships today; next-gen Proteus is the platform bet. Market cap US$145-160m at $0.73 against $169.9m of cash and marketable securities at 30-Jun-2026 - the equity trades below net cash because the Proteus launch slipped to Q2 2027.
why_10x: 10x = $1.60bn. Proteus must ship on time in Q2 2027 and convert to instrument-plus-consumable revenue; at $80-120m of revenue growing 50%+, tools platforms trade at 12-20x sales. Detection on CMOS means the cost curve should follow Moore's law, as Ion Torrent's did, not a mass spectrometer's. A newly disclosed >$4bn non-human proteomics TAM (agri, pathogen typing, viral surveillance) widens the frame beyond the original clinical pitch. 100x = $16.0bn (~45% of Illumina) is arithmetically conceivable but a tail, not a plan.
what_kills_it: Proteus read length, accuracy and throughput may not beat mass spec on real biological questions - the extra design cycle and 20% reduction in force say management is not yet confident in manufacturing readiness. A second slip at $0.73 invites Nasdaq minimum-bid trouble and a reverse split. Class B super-voting stock (19.94m shares x 20 votes = ~66.7% of votes, own calc from the 10-Q cover, 2026-08-11) leaves minorities no recourse.

name: Caribou Biosciences, Inc.
thesis: Off-the-shelf allogeneic CAR-T using proprietary chRDNA (hybrid DNA-RNA guide) editing, co-founded by Jennifer Doudna. Market cap US$134m at $1.25 against $113.8m of cash and marketable securities and $26.7m of debt, i.e. an enterprise value of roughly $45m - the market ascribes almost nothing to a platform that has FDA alignment on a pivotal Phase 3 design.
why_10x: 10x = $1.33bn. The evidence is far better than the price: at EHA 2026, optimised vispa-cel (80m cells, donor <30, >=2 matched HLA alleles, n=27) in 2L LBCL gave 82% ORR, 67% CR and 17.1-month median PFS; CB-011 at the 450m-cell expansion dose in 12 BCMA-naive myeloma patients gave 92% ORR, 83% >=CR, 91% MRD-negativity and 50% still in >=CR at 15 months (Q2 release, 2026-08-13). FDA has agreed ANTLER-3: ~250 CD19-naive 2L LBCL patients who cannot access autologous CAR-T - a population incumbents structurally cannot serve. From a $45m EV the first 3x is just the market ceasing to price liquidation. 100x = $13.3bn improbable: $113.8m cannot fund two registrational programmes, so a partner takes half the economics.
what_kills_it: Allogeneic durability - the classic failure is host rejection, responses looking excellent at 3-6 months and collapsing by 18; 17.1-month median PFS is Phase 1, n=27, single-arm. The funding gap: management is explicitly 'exploring multiple options to fully fund' ANTLER-3, so a 250-patient Phase 3 means handing away the asset or destroying the share count. In-vivo CAR-T (Capstan/AbbVie, Umoja) could make ex-vivo allogeneic obsolete before approval.

name: Cellectis S.A.
thesis: TALEN gene-editing pioneer and allogeneic CAR-T developer, now roughly 44% owned by AstraZeneca. Market cap ~US$142m at EUR1.151 against $188m of cash and fixed-term deposits at 31-Mar-2026 with runway into Q4 2027. Own clinical programmes lasme-cel (r/r B-ALL) and eti-cel (r/r NHL) both read out in Q4 2026.
why_10x: 10x = $1.42bn; Cellectis traded above $1.5bn in 2021 on weaker evidence. The arithmetic that makes this defensible: AstraZeneca paid $5.00 per preferred share for its stake, while the ordinary line closed at EUR1.151 (~$1.32) on 2026-09-16 - AZ is roughly 74% underwater on equity it bought after diligence, and you are offered the same asset at about a quarter of its price. With cash above market cap at the last report, the first ~1.5x needs nothing but the market ceasing to price the equity below net cash; the remaining ~7x needs one Q4 2026 clinical success or one AZ programme entering the clinic. 100x = $14.2bn is the wrong bet - AZ's 44% means minorities capture a fraction.
what_kills_it: The 44% stake cuts both ways - AZ can block, dictate terms or low-ball the minority, and preferred structures can rank ahead of ordinary shareholders. A decade in the clinic without a breakout dataset; persistence and host rejection remain unsolved, and Q4 2026 is where that gets tested. Thin liquidity (~EUR340k/day median, the thinnest of its group) and a weakening balance sheet - cash and equivalents down to $35.6m against $84.6m of debt at 30-Jun-2026.

name: Fractyl Health, Inc.
thesis: Two assets attacking metabolic disease at the organ, not the hormone: Revita, a 45-minute endoscopic duodenal resurfacing procedure to stop weight regain after GLP-1 discontinuation, and Rejuva, a pancreatic gene-therapy platform making islet cells produce incretins endogenously. Market cap US$89.6m at $0.563. A genuine binary deliberately funded only to the pivotal readout. MATERIAL: on 2026-09-10 Nasdaq notified Fractyl its securities are subject to delisting after it failed to regain $1.00 minimum bid compliance by 2026-09-09; a Hearings Panel request stays suspension (8-K filed 2026-09-11), and this is material to whether the position stays holdable on ii.
why_10x: 10x = $0.90bn. The randomised evidence is stronger than the price implies: in the REMAIN-1 Midpoint Cohort at one year, in the pre-specified optimised population (complete ablation >14cm plus run-in loss >=17.5%), Revita patients maintained ~84% of prior GLP-1-induced weight loss versus 46% for sham - LSM regain 4.1% vs 13.5% (n=10 vs 8) - with no device- or procedure-related SAEs through one year; REVEAL-1 open-label at one year (n=15) maintained ~78%. The dose-response concentration of benefit where ablation was complete is mechanistic, not post-hoc luck. Durability is the largest unmet need in medicine's largest market. 100x = $9.0bn is below where single-asset obesity companies have traded pre-approval, so it is arithmetically live - but dilution defeats it.
what_kills_it: REMAIN-1 Pivotal misses - sham-controlled device trials fail often and the Midpoint result came from an optimised subgroup of 18 patients. The capital structure: $47.1m cash against $60.7m of debt and stockholders' equity of MINUS $1.7m at 30-Jun-2026, runway only into early 2027 - lenders sit ahead of shareholders, and a miss means equity holders are wiped out. Delisting: if the Hearings Panel is not persuaded the shares leave Nasdaq, and OTC is outside the ii mandate entirely.

name: Prime Medicine, Inc.
thesis: Prime Medicine develops prime editing - a search-and-replace genome edit that nicks one DNA strand and writes a new sequence from an attached template, with no double-strand break and no donor DNA. In principle it can correct the large majority of known pathogenic human variants rather than the narrow subset addressable by base editing or by knocking a gene out, which is where the volume of human genetic disease actually lives. This is no longer a preclinical claim: PM359 produced clinical proof of prime editing in humans, the FDA granted it RMAT designation on 2026-06-22, and a BLA is targeted for the first half of 2027. Cash and investments of US$108.8m at 30-Jun-2026 against a ~US$42m quarterly loss make a financing inside the holding period close to certain.
why_10x: 10x = US$5.44bn. The required chain is specific: PM359 approved or clearly approvable, PM577a showing durable in vivo correction in Wilson disease with clean safety, and at least one large-pharma deal on an in vivo programme. That combination would make Prime the only company with a clinically validated, correction-capable editor - and editing platforms have carried US$5-10bn valuations on thinner evidence (Intellia peaked above US$10bn in 2021 on a single interim). The multiple is not the stretch; surviving the financing with the share count intact is. 100x = US$54.4bn is Vertex-scale and requires commercial infrastructure Prime cannot fund; the realistic terminal event is an acquisition in the US$5-15bn band. Note dilution cuts the per-share multiple: a US$5.4bn enterprise reached after two raises might deliver 6-7x on today's price.
what_kills_it: The financing, at this price - US$108.8m against a ~US$42m quarterly loss and an 'into 2027' guide means raising from a share price 57% off its high. This is the most likely way to be right and still lose money. Translation: ex vivo success in CGD says little about whether a prime editor delivered to the liver corrects enough hepatocytes to change a Wilson disease phenotype, and the 2027 PM577a readout is a genuine binary. Category risk - gene-editing equities have de-rated as a group and even good data has repeatedly failed to re-rate them.

name: ProQR Therapeutics N.V.
thesis: RNA-editing company whose Axiomer platform uses chemically modified oligonucleotides to recruit the body's own ADAR enzymes for a single A-to-I edit in a target mRNA. Market cap US$262.5m at $1.86 against EUR117.1m (~$134m) of cash at 30-Jun-2026 and runway into mid-2028 - roughly half the market value is cash, so the platform, two clinical assets and the Lilly package are valued at about $144m.
why_10x: 10x = $2.63bn. The key upgrade versus the candidate record: the first human editing signal is no longer a future catalyst, it has already happened. In June 2026 AX-0810 Phase 1 delivered up to an 8-fold increase in total serum bile acids at 6 mg/kg against a pre-defined 2-fold threshold - clearing its own bar by 4x - with dose-dependent conjugated bile acid changes, no serious adverse events, no pruritus and an eight-week half-life, which the company calls the first clinical validation of Axiomer. Axiomer is the pragmatic middle ground: re-dosable, reversible, no viral vector or LNP, using GalNAc delivery that already works commercially. Wave traded above $1bn on ADAR proof-of-concept alone. 100x = $26.6bn: NO - ProQR has partnered its biggest opportunities to Lilly and takes royalties.
what_kills_it: Target engagement is not efficacy - bile-acid movement in healthy volunteers is a biomarker, and Korro's 2026 KRRO-110 failure is the direct precedent for a similar mechanism disappointing at the patient stage. Liver-only delivery: GalNAc works and nothing else does yet, capping indications until extrahepatic delivery is solved. Lilly can walk, and ProQR has a long failure history - sepofarsen and ultevursen both failed and the company has already pivoted itself once.

name: Median Technologies SA
thesis: AI Software-as-a-Medical-Device for lung cancer screening. eyonis LCS detects AND characterises lung nodules on low-dose CT - a combined CADe/CADx device, not just nodule-finding. Market cap ~US$231m at EUR3.785. Two caveats up front: this is Euronext GROWTH (a junior MTF, not main Euronext Paris) and ii's coverage of that venue was NOT confirmed - check on ii.co.uk before committing capital; and the balance sheet is the weakest in its group.
why_10x: 10x = $2.32bn, and this is the cleanest arithmetic in the sleeve because CMS has already set the price per unit. FDA 510(k) clearance was granted 2026-02-09 and CMS New Tech APC reimbursement pays approximately $601-700 per exam for 2026, against ~14.5 million Americans meeting USPSTF screening criteria. At ~$600/exam with software gross margins, one million exams is ~$600m of revenue; even 500,000 exams a year is ~$300m of very high-margin revenue, which at 7-8x sales is ~$2.3bn. A cleared device that already has a payment code and a per-exam price is a different asset class from an AI company hoping for one. 100x = $23bn: NO, that implies $2-3bn of annual revenue from a single screening indication.
what_kills_it: Adoption, not technology - radiology procurement cycles are long, and Aidence/RadNet, Optellum, Coreline and the Siemens/GE in-house tools are already inside the workflow. The balance sheet, which is the likeliest way to lose money here: stockholders' equity of MINUS EUR35.2m at 31-Dec-2025, more debt (EUR21.8-25.3m) than cash (EUR18.2-18.4m), and shares up from 18.42m (Dec-2024) to 49.00m now - +166% in ~21 months. Venue and reimbursement risk - Euronext Growth means lighter disclosure and ~EUR550k/day liquidity, and New Tech APC rates are reviewed annually and can fall.

name: Clarity Pharmaceuticals Ltd
thesis: Copper-64/copper-67 radiopharmaceutical theranostics using the proprietary SAR sarcophagine chelator. Lead 64Cu-SAR-bisPSMA is a prostate-cancer PET imaging agent in registrational Phase 3 (CLARIFY); the matched therapeutic 67Cu-SAR-bisPSMA uses the same targeting molecule. Market cap ~US$558m at A$2.09, debt-free with A$178.3m of reported cash. SCEPTIC'S FIRST QUESTION, FLAGGED HONESTLY: the shares are down roughly 63% from a 52-week high of A$5.70 and sit ~15% above the 52-week low; the cause of that de-rating could NOT be established from the sources reachable this session - read Clarity's 2026 ASX announcements before acting.
why_10x: 10x = US$5.58bn. The mechanism is a manufacturing and logistics advantage, not just chemistry: gallium-68's 68-minute half-life forces production beside the patient, whereas copper-64's 12.7-hour half-life and Clarity's stated 48-hour shelf life allow central manufacture and overnight shipping, and next-day imaging when background has cleared - which is why the CLARIFY protocol images at Day 1 and Day 2. The SAR cage holds copper tightly enough not to leak in vivo, which is what previously made copper unusable. And the same molecule carries copper-67 for therapy, giving identical biodistribution a gallium/lutetium pair can never guarantee. Precedents: BMS paid ~$4.1bn for RayzeBio and AstraZeneca ~$2.4bn for Fusion, both pre-approval. 100x = US$55.8bn: NO - that exceeds the entire current radiopharmaceutical industry.
what_kills_it: The comparator, not the agent - CLARIFY's endpoint is sensitivity and specificity for pelvic nodal disease against surgical pathology in 383 high-risk patients going to radical prostatectomy with lymph node dissection, a brutal standard on which imaging trials fail even when the agent works. Radiochemistry at scale - copper-64 supply and manufacturing scale-up is a genuine risk, and the 48-hour shelf-life advantage only exists if production is reliable. Entrenched competition (Novartis, Lantheus, Telix) plus a demanding starting price: at ~$558m the shares already discount considerable success, and the unexplained 63% drawdown means the market may know something this dossier does not.

name: SEALSQ Corp
thesis: Swiss designer of secure microcontrollers and hardware security modules converting its franchise to post-quantum: the QS7001 Quantum Shield secure element and QVault TPM implement NIST post-quantum algorithms in hardware. The central fact: market cap US$489m at $2.19 against $486.1m of cash at 30-Jun-2026 and $7.1m of debt - an enterprise value of roughly $14m for a business guided to $27-36m of FY2026 revenue growing 131% at ~48% gross margin with a >$225m pipeline. Either the market believes the cash will be destroyed, or this is mispriced; both readings deserve respect.
why_10x: 10x = $4.89bn, but with $486.1m of cash in hand the operating business only has to be worth ~$4.4bn - and it does not need to raise again to get there. Post-quantum cryptography cannot live only in software: firmware signing, secure boot and device identity must be rooted in hardware, so every one of the tens of billions of connected devices shipped this decade needs a root of trust running algorithms that did not exist when today's secure elements were designed. That is a forced, dated replacement cycle driven by regulation (EU Cyber Resilience Act, US federal migration timetables). Hardware root-of-trust is a certification moat: QS7001 has NIST SP 800-90B Entropy Source Validation and has completed Common Criteria testing. Revenue must go from ~$30m to $300-400m. 100x = $49bn: NO, that is Infineon scale.
what_kills_it: The dilution record is the thesis risk - that $486m was raised by issuing shares, with the count going from 101.54m (31-Dec-2024) to 224.93m (30-Jun-2026), +121.5% in 18 months, and nothing stops it continuing; cash per share, not cash, is what you own. Governance - WISeKey's voting control through non-traded Class F shares means minorities cannot object to related-party transactions, and the group has a history of them (Wecan, Quobly, Miraex). Infineon, NXP and STMicroelectronics will all ship post-quantum secure elements and own the automotive design-in relationships.

name: Terrestrial Energy Inc.
thesis: Terrestrial Energy develops the Integral Molten Salt Reactor - 390 MWt / ~195 MWe delivering 585C process heat, with the whole primary loop inside a sealed, replaceable seven-year Core-unit. Nasdaq-listed via the HCM II de-SPAC, development site at Texas A&M-RELLIS. Trading at $4.25 against a $31.50 52-week high while licensing evidence accumulates. Not flagged by the fact-checker.
why_10x: 10x on ~US$352m is US$3.5bn, requiring a construction permit application docketed and accepted, one binding multi-GW offtake, and a demonstrated LEU fuel-salt supply chain. On the company's stated ~US$2.7bn lifetime revenue per plant, an 8-12 plant pipeline implies a US$22-32bn backlog; the market paid US$5-8bn for less in this sector before the 2026 de-rating. Two structural choices matter: the sealed Core-unit sidesteps 60-year component corrosion, and IMSR runs on standard-assay LEU rather than HALEU, avoiding the enrichment bottleneck gating Oklo and X-energy. 100x is not conceivable in the hold period.
what_kills_it: Molten-salt chemistry - tritium permeation, fission-product management and salt corrosion defeated every programme since Oak Ridge's MSRE, and no molten-salt reactor has ever been NRC-licensed, so the review timetable is open-ended. The Riot Platforms deal is an MOU, not a contract. Construction-stage dilution: US$283m does not build a reactor, and the raise that funds first concrete comes from a register nursing a 93% drawdown.

name: EMVision Medical Devices Ltd
thesis: EMVision is developing emu, a portable electromagnetic brain-imaging device for pre-hospital and bedside stroke triage - distinguishing haemorrhagic from ischaemic stroke at the point of care, which currently requires a CT scanner. A pivotal trial is running inside live code-stroke workflows at eight leading academic centres. Not flagged by the fact-checker.
why_10x: 10x is ~US$1.09bn. The pivotal trial must clear 80% sensitivity and specificity, the FDA must grant De Novo clearance, and emu must sell into US stroke centres and ambulance fleets. Roughly 1,800 certified US stroke centres and tens of thousands of ambulances at a US$100-200k device price plus service means a few thousand units is US$300-500m of revenue; a cleared, category-creating device with that installed base supports US$1bn+ (Inspire Medical and Shockwave both passed it shortly after clearance). 100x (US$10.9bn) is arithmetically possible on the Shockwave path but assumes EMVision is not acquired long before.
what_kills_it: Binary trial risk - miss 80% sensitivity or specificity and the product is not clinically usable; the company is blinded until recruitment completes, so there is no early warning. No regulatory precedent: electromagnetic brain imaging has never been FDA-cleared, so De Novo timing and evidentiary demands are unknown. Liquidity - at roughly A$56k of average daily traded value this is the thinnest name in the sleeve after HyTerra and Gelion; the price will gap in both directions and cannot be exited quickly.

name: Solid Power, Inc.
thesis: Solid Power is pivoting from being a cell maker to being the merchant supplier of sulphide solid electrolyte - the scarce input every solid-state battery programme needs - with BMW building Solid Power cells on its own line and SK On having purchased and installed a Solid Power-built electrolyte pilot line. About 71% of the market cap is cash, so the market values the technology near zero. Not flagged by the fact-checker.
why_10x: 10x is US$5.83bn. It requires the electrolyte business to convert from pilot to merchant supply with at least two named offtakes, and one automaker to commit solid-state to a production vehicle programme. At scale sulphide electrolyte is plausibly a US$500m-1bn annual revenue line at chemical-specialty margins, and US$5.8bn is 6-10x that - what sole-source battery-materials suppliers command. 100x (US$58bn) is not credible: more than the market value of any battery-materials company outside China.
what_kills_it: Revenue that goes backwards - Q2 2026 revenue was negative US$268k on changed milestones, which says the customer relationships are not yet contractual annuities. Being designed out: automakers have a long record of internalising battery chemistry once it works, and the Joint Evaluation Agreement structure makes that easy for BMW, SK On or Samsung SDI. The market may simply be right - solid-state timelines have slipped across the industry before.

name: HyTerra Ltd
thesis: HyTerra is a sub-cent ASX natural-hydrogen explorer on the Nemaha Ridge in Kansas with ~80,000 acres, plus a 16% earn-in on the Geneva Project in Nebraska. The dossier already withdrew two backer claims the candidate record carried: Fortescue could not be found anywhere on HyTerra's site or news archive (checked 2026-09-17) and is treated as unconfirmed, and the widely circulated Mitsubishi Gas Chemical / Toyota / Eneos story concerns Gold Hydrogen, a different ASX company, not HyTerra. This is the smallest position in the sleeve at US$7.6m and the purest lottery ticket in it.
why_10x: 10x is only ~US$76m (about A$107m) - in an exploration play that is one well demonstrating sustained commercial-rate hydrogen flow in Kansas, re-rating this from pre-discovery explorer to holder of a proven North American natural hydrogen field. That is a routine magnitude of move for a microcap explorer on discovery (Helix Exploration and Pulsar Helium both did comparable moves on helium). The requirement is flow rate, not concentration. 100x (US$760m) is arithmetically the clearest case in the sleeve: a proven, developable geologic hydrogen field with 80,000 surrounding acres in a US industrial corridor plus helium credits is plausibly worth that - Koloma was privately valued in that region without a proven producing field.
what_kills_it: The play type may simply not work - no one has ever commercially produced natural hydrogen at scale, and concentration measurements are not flow rates. The raise: roughly twelve months of cash on 2.14bn shares at A$0.005 means the next placement will be brutally dilutive, and sub-cent ASX microcaps have a very high base rate of permanent capital loss. The best result is not theirs - the 44% hydrogen / 13% helium Hoarty NE3 figure comes from a well HyTerra holds only 16% of, not from its 100%-owned flagship.

name: Satellos Bioscience Inc.
thesis: Satellos Bioscience is developing SAT-3247, an oral, mutation-agnostic small molecule that restores satellite-cell polarity to regenerate muscle in Duchenne muscular dystrophy - addressing all DMD genotypes rather than the subsets served by exon-skipping and gene therapy. Dual-listed TSX and Nasdaq, funded to the pivotal readout with C$61.8m. Not flagged by the fact-checker.
why_10x: 10x is ~US$2.03bn. BASECAMP must show functional benefit - not just biomarker movement - in placebo-controlled paediatric patients. A mutation-agnostic oral therapy for all DMD patients addresses roughly 20,000 people in the US and EU at orphan pricing: a US$1-2bn peak-sales asset. Sarepta exceeded US$10bn on a franchise serving only a fraction of genotypes, so US$2bn for an oral serving all of them is conservative if the drug works. 100x (US$20bn) needs SAT-3247 to succeed in DMD and translate into sarcopenia or GLP-1-associated muscle loss; the mechanism supports the read-across but Satellos cannot currently fund that second indication.
what_kills_it: The interim data are the weakest form of evidence - TRAILHEAD is open-label, and the blinded Q4 2026 paediatric readout can easily fail; DMD trials are notoriously hard to power on functional endpoints in small paediatric cohorts. The hypothesis has never produced an approved drug - satellite-cell polarity restoration has zero regulatory precedent. Funded to the data, not through it: C$61.8m against a C$11.7m quarterly loss funds the readout and about a year beyond, so a negative or ambiguous result means the next raise is at a fraction of today's price.

name: Robosense Technology Co., Ltd
thesis: RoboSense is China's largest lidar maker by volume, deliberately re-pointing from cars to robots and selling the whole humanoid sensing-and-motion bill of materials: eyes (lidar, Space Camera), skin (visuo-tactile and MEMS tactile sensors) and muscles (joint modules, actuators). The conversion is already in the numbers: H1 2026 revenue RMB 1.02bn (+30.2% YoY), total lidar shipments 719,200 units (+169.6%) and robotics lidar shipments 282,600 units (+510.4% YoY) (2026 interim results, PR Newswire, 2026-08-26), against a stock at HK$16.09 versus a HK$46.50 52-week high. Fact-check correction: Cainiao is described as a top-two pre-IPO shareholder, the previously claimed 'largest, 10.46%' having been withdrawn as uncorroborated.
why_10x: 10x on ~US$946m is ~US$9.5bn: roughly RMB 8-12bn of revenue at 5-8x sales (four to six times the current run-rate) with robotics carrying 40%+ gross margins. The mechanism is concrete - one to two million humanoid and service robots a year, each taking US$1,500-3,000 of RoboSense sensing and actuation content - and RoboSense is the only listed company selling all three layers. The tactile skin matters more than the lidar: higher ASP, far less commoditised, and a MEMS tactile sensor that does not drift is the unsolved problem in dexterous manipulation. 100x (US$95bn) is not possible; the constraint is geopolitical, not arithmetic.
what_kills_it: The ADAS lidar price war eats the funding base - ASPs around RMB 1,000 and falling against a 24.5% gross margin; if automotive losses widen faster than robotics margin arrives, the IPO cash is consumed before the transition completes. Export controls or entity listing close the Western market, and China alone will not support a 10x multiple; plus HKEX settlement and geopolitical risk for a UK holder. Humanoid demand may be state subsidy rather than demand, and vision-based software may solve tactile sensing more cheaply than hardware, stranding the skin investment.

name: General Fusion Group Ltd.
thesis: General Fusion is the only listed pure-play fusion company (Magnetised Target Fusion; LM26 machine in Richmond BC), de-SPACed 2026-07-13 and trading at roughly half its debut price. CORRECTED AT FACT-CHECK: the ~US$135m post-close cash and ~3-year runway stand, but the market cap did not. The F-1 contradicts itself (53,132,058 SVS on the cover vs 63,548,721 SVS plus 10,416,663 MVS in the ownership section, same date); yfinance's 80,723,040 shares / US$631m matches no filing and has been removed as a Yahoo data trap. Corrected market cap ~US$498m at the $7.84 close, corroborated by stockanalysis.com. ADV also corrected to a 20-day ~US$1.35m/day.
why_10x: Scarcity of listed access plus documented Canadian state backing: BDC Capital (a wholly owned subsidiary of the Business Development Bank of Canada, a federal Crown corporation) holds 3,287,483 shares and 9,076,980 warrants, and a Strategic Innovation Fund contribution agreement with the Minister of Industry has been amended through January 2025. The 10x has been recomputed honestly and is harder than the previous draft claimed: a 10x in the SHARE PRICE ($7.84 to $78.40) converts the Multiple Voting Shares (up to 44,810,873 SVS) and the Earnout Shares (11,978,950) and puts every warrant in the money, implying a US$9.4bn company on that base and ~US$13.6bn fully diluted (173.5m shares) - not US$6.3bn. That is roughly twice the largest private fusion comparable, so a pure re-rating toward private peers delivers perhaps 3-5x; the 10x needs a genuine scientific or state-award event.
what_kills_it: The physics - MTF has never reached breakeven, and the company concedes liquid-liner compression has not been demonstrated at power-plant-relevant scale. Dilution: the F-1 offers 109,928,827 SVS issuable by the company and registers 102,262,208 SVS issuable on exercise/conversion for resale - ~173% of shares outstanding - with PIPE MVS converting at an assumed $5.00 plus maximum accrued-value increase through the fifth anniversary of closing. Being second: first-of-a-kind plant not before the mid-2030s; if CFS or Helion reaches net energy first, MTF is a stranded science project.

name: Archer Materials Limited
thesis: Archer Materials runs two independent semiconductor programmes on the same carbon/graphene device physics: 12CQ, a qubit processor chip designed to hold and read an electron spin at ROOM TEMPERATURE, and a graphene field-effect biochip for point-of-care blood chemistry. The quantum claim attacks cost-per-qubit rather than qubit count - the cryogenic bill of materials, not the qubit count, is what makes quantum computers cost tens of millions each. At US$37.3m it is the cheapest position in the sleeve in absolute dollars, with A$10.3m of cash at March 2026 and no debt. On 2026-06-30 it signed a three-year Quantum Compute Agreement with IonQ - but note the direction of the money: Archer PAYS IonQ US$1.5m over three years for Forte/Tempo-class access and reselling rights, so this is commercial intent, not a backer.
why_10x: 10x = ~US$373m (A$525m), reachable by either of two independent routes. Quantum route: a working room-temperature spin readout at wafer scale turns 12CQ into licensable IP rather than a hardware competitor, and listed quantum names with no revenue and one credible physics claim have carried A$400m-1bn valuations this cycle. Biochip route: a CLIA-validated point-of-care potassium chip is a real medical-device business (dialysis, cardiology, emergency medicine) and such companies routinely reach A$300-600m with a cleared product and a partner. 100x = ~US$3.7bn is possible only if 12CQ becomes standard IP inside other people's machines - not underwritten, but not absurd from US$37m.
what_kills_it: The physics simply does not close - room-temperature spin coherence in carbon has been 'close' for years, and a 2026 demonstrator that fails to read out a single spin removes the entire quantum leg. Dilution is the base case, not a risk: A$10.3m against a two-programme R&D cost base plus US$500k a year payable to IonQ means raising into whatever price the demonstrator produces. And nobody is aligned - 1.1% institutional, no strategic investor and no anchor shareholder, which for an extraordinary physics claim is itself evidence a sceptic may weigh. Liquidity of ~US$111k/day means the position cannot be exited into bad news.

name: Molecular Partners AG
thesis: DARPins are near-ideal vectors for short-lived alpha emitters: a tenth the mass of an antibody, antibody-like affinity, thermostable, with a tunable half-life long enough to reach tumour and short enough to clear before marrow takes the dose. Orano Med, the principal industrial producer of lead-212, chose DARPins and now co-develops TEN programmes (MP0712 212Pb/DLL3 in clinic, MP0714 225Ac, MP0726 MSLN), an endorsement from the party controlling isotope supply. Market cap CHF124.5m against CHF67.9m cash leaves an EV of roughly CHF60m for three clinical assets plus secured isotope access.
why_10x: 10x = CHF1.25bn (~$1.5bn). From a CHF60m EV, most of the return is the platform being priced at all. Requires MP0712 tumour responses in SCLC with tolerable marrow toxicity. Comparables acquired pre-approval on early data: Point $1.4bn, Fusion $2.4bn, RayzeBio $4.1bn. 100x (CHF12.5bn) is not credible - the declared strategy is partnering and Orano co-owns the lead economics.
what_kills_it: Management destroyed most of the company's value twice already (abicipar failed at FDA with Novartis; ensovibep abandoned). Alpha-emitter renal/marrow toxicity appears only at higher doses - cohort 1 cleanliness at 75 MBq says nothing about 105 MBq+. Lead-212 supply concentrated in one partner: both moat and single point of failure. Plus ~$65k/day SIX liquidity.

name: Li-S Energy Limited
thesis: Lithium-sulphur/lithium-metal cell maker in Brisbane using boron nitride nanotubes to attack dendrite formation and polysulphide shuttling simultaneously, with captive BNNT supply via PPK. It has stopped being a science project: it shipped its first cells to US Army DEVCOM in June 2026. Li-S wins first where mass is the binding constraint - high-altitude UAVs, undersea autonomy - not where cost per kWh is. Now vertically integrated into lithium foil, a genuine Western supply gap.
why_10x: 10x = US$683m (~A$960m). Requires one defence relationship converting to a multi-year supply programme worth A$50-100m annually plus foil revenue; ASX battery-materials names with defence offtakes have been paid 8-12x revenue, implying A$80-120m of revenue visibility. 100x (US$6.8bn) is not possible: a single Phase 3 line with a ~A$6m cost base cannot become a global cell maker without raises that destroy the multiple.
what_kills_it: Cycle life - every Li-S programme in history has died here and nothing public proves the BNNT cell survives at defence-qualification standard. Evaluation orders usually go nowhere; DEVCOM shipments are cheap for the Army and existential for the company. The 69.5% insider block is also an overhang and governance concentration (the PPK related-party structure has drawn scrutiny), with ~US$18k/day turnover making the position effectively unsellable in stress.

name: GSI Technology, Inc.
thesis: Thirty-year SRAM maker funding the Associative Processing Unit, a compute-in-memory chip that does search and inference inside the memory array. The mechanism is the memory wall: inference cost is dominated by moving weights and vectors, not arithmetic, and computing in-array removes the movement rather than accelerating it - largest advantage exactly for retrieval, similarity and vector search, now the default enterprise AI pattern. Unlike compute-in-memory startups, GSI already owns the memory process and holds radiation-tolerant defence variants; Gemini-II passed radiation testing July 2026.
why_10x: 10x = $1.85bn. Gemini-II must win a repeatable design - a programme of record or a datacentre retrieval accelerator - taking revenue from $25m to $200-300m at APU gross margins. At ~$1.8bn it would be a credible compute-in-memory challenger, still below where private peers d-Matrix and EnCharge have raised. 100x ($18.5bn) is not credible: a declining SRAM annuity plus one architecture does not become a platform vendor; 20x is the tail case.
what_kills_it: Gemini-I is the precedent and it failed commercially - the barrier was never silicon but the difficulty of programming a non-von-Neumann architecture; if the September 2026 AI SDK doesn't change that, nothing will. The legacy SRAM base is structurally shrinking and Q1 FY2027 revenue was already flat y/y. d-Matrix and EnCharge attack the same wall with far more capital, and further dilution is likely after the +31.9% share-count increase already absorbed.

name: BioAge Labs, Inc.
thesis: BioAge mines 30-year prospective human longevity cohorts - samples banked before disease onset, outcomes recorded decades later - to back-solve causal ageing biology into drug targets. You cannot buy or build such a cohort in under 30 years, which is a temporal moat. Lead asset BGE-102 is an oral, brain-penetrant NLRP3 inhibitor that produced median ~86% hsCRP reductions at 60mg and 120mg in Phase 1 with consistent IL-6 and fibrinogen falls. $381.3m of cash and securities at 30-Jun-2026 against a $355.8m market cap means the market values the entire pipeline below zero.
why_10x: 10x = $3.56bn. BGE-102 must convert an 86% hsCRP reduction into a clinical endpoint - visual acuity in DME or weight/inflammation benefit adjunctive to GLP-1s - and be partnered with Novartis or Lilly at billion-dollar economics. Large pharma has repeatedly paid up for oral NLRP3; a best-in-class brain-penetrant version with Ph2 data supports $3-5bn, and with a negative starting EV essentially all of it is pipeline recognition. 100x ($35.6bn) would need statin-scale chronic use with BioAge owning the economics - it has no commercial infrastructure and a declared partnering strategy.
what_kills_it: It has already lost a lead asset - azelaprag discontinued on liver transaminitis in STRIDES Ph2. NLRP3 has a poor clinical record: the class repeatedly produces beautiful biomarker data then fails on hepatotoxicity or efficacy; hsCRP reduction is not clinical benefit. 2.4% insider ownership with a 90.5% institutional register means no internal skin in the game and violent moves on fund exits - the $4.90-$25.10 52-week range proves it.

name: Airship AI Holdings, Inc.
thesis: AI video and sensor data management (Outpost AI edge devices, Acropolis, Airship Command) already deployed inside DoJ and DHS environments. The moat is accreditation, not algorithms: Airship has cleared the security, procurement-vehicle and integration hurdles that keep better-funded commercial AI vendors out for years, and edge processing is the architecturally correct answer for agencies that cannot send video to a commercial cloud. A 75% gross margin on a hardware-inclusive product is the evidence the software does the work. At ~3.1x EV/sales with a $206m validated pipeline, one programme of record changes the company.
why_10x: 10x = $656m. Needs revenue of $90-120m - five to seven times current - at 70%+ gross margin on a 6-8x sales multiple, realistically via one large multi-year federal programme (~$50m+) plus a commercial channel. Airship's whole value is being pre-positioned for exactly that award. 100x ($6.6bn) is arithmetically conceivable but would put it alongside the largest public-safety software vendors with decades of installed base; I would not underwrite it.
what_kills_it: Revenue is small, lumpy and government-dependent - Q1 FY26 $6.35m fell to $4.12m in Q2, a 35% sequential drop; a continuing resolution or lost recompete removes a large share. Palantir, Axon and Motorola Solutions compete in exactly this segment with the relationships, accreditations and far more capital. SPAC legacy: warrant/PIPE overhang, reported GAAP profit is a derivative fair-value artefact (operating income negative in all last five quarters), and the stock is down 63% in a year.

name: Filtronic plc
thesis: Filtronic is the sole qualified external supplier of E-band solid-state power amplifiers into SpaceX's Starlink ground gateways, plus mmWave transceivers for European defence EW and space primes, manufactured ITAR-free in the UK. The moat is qualification: SpaceX does not re-qualify a flight-critical RF part casually, and its revealed preference was to take warrants rather than vertically integrate. Order flow proves the cycle - $62.5m SpaceX (Aug 2025), GBP13.4m defence prime (Jul 2025), EUR7m constellation (Nov 2025), $8.0m US (Mar 2026), $8m follow-on as recently as 2026-09-16. The only profitable, cash-generative, net-cash name in the sleeve.
why_10x: 10x = ~$6.9bn (GBP5.2bn). On GBP55.5m of revenue that needs GBP400-600m at an 8-12x sales multiple, roughly a ten-fold volume increase, achieved by becoming the mmWave front-end supplier to multiple constellations (Starlink, Kuiper, IRIS2) AND European EW simultaneously - several fabs' worth of capacity, so expect capex and dilution en route. 100x ($69bn) is impossible: even at 100% share of every Western gateway amplifier the revenue does not support it.
what_kills_it: Total customer concentration - SpaceX can insource E-band amplifiers at any point and the warrants would be all shareholders got. The customer appears to hold the pricing power: EBITDA fell from GBP8.7m to GBP5.1m on flat revenue while SpaceX volumes expanded; management calls it deliberate investment, a sceptic calls it margin transfer. Warrant dilution of up to 15%, plus lumpy gateway build-out where a single pause shows in the next half immediately.

name: BTQ Technologies Corp.
thesis: Full-stack 'trusted quantum': neutral-atom emulation/digital-twin/control via the completed QPerfect acquisition, the QSSN post-quantum security stack, and Bitcoin Quantum - a quantum-safe Bitcoin fork using NIST-standardised signatures. The mechanism is a forced migration with a deadline: 6-7m BTC sit in address types with public keys already exposed on-chain, NIST has finalised FIPS 203/204/205, and national timetables run to 2030-2035. BTQ is the only listed company that has shipped a working quantum-safe Bitcoin testnet - 75+ miners, 300,000+ blocks, 150+ open-source contributors - rather than a whitepaper.
why_10x: 10x = ~$3.87bn. Bitcoin Quantum must launch and be adopted by a meaningful share of miners plus at least one large custodian or exchange, with QSSN converting a flagship enterprise contract to recurring revenue. At ~$3.9bn the market would value BTQ as critical infrastructure for the post-quantum migration of digital assets - an adoption-and-narrative re-rate, not an earnings one, since revenue would still be small. 100x ($38.7bn) is not credible: larger than almost every listed quantum and crypto-infrastructure company combined, on a share count that must keep rising.
what_kills_it: The Bitcoin community rejects the fork - forks without social consensus die (BCH, BSV) and Bitcoin governance is structurally hostile to outside commercial actors; 75 testnet miners is not social consensus. FINANCING RISK IS ACUTE - C$9.73m cash at 30-Jun-2026 against a C$5.94m quarterly burn is ~1.6 quarters; BTQ must issue equity into a stock already 81% below its high, and each raise compounds the share count against any 10x. Priced entirely on narrative - $387m market cap on $0 revenue means it de-rates with the quantum complex regardless of execution, with founder control at 35%.

name: Bango PLC
thesis: Bango's Digital Vending Machine is the entitlement, provisioning, revenue-share, tax and cancellation plumbing under subscription bundling, plus the direct carrier billing rails. It is a genuine two-sided network - content owners integrate once to reach every operator, operators integrate once to reach every content owner - and network effects at a GBP48m market cap are rare. Four independent blue-chip validations in six months of 2026: KDDI, Telin/LMT, LinkedIn and Turkcell. It trades at 1.24x EV/sales on an 84.5% gross margin.
why_10x: 10x = ~$643m (GBP480m). Needs annualised recurring revenue of roughly $120-150m at 30%+ EBITDA margins on a 4-5x sales multiple, with the DVM becoming the default bundling layer for 30-40 large operators rather than a dozen, and at least one hyperscaler AI subscription distributed through it. The network effect makes adoption non-linear - the last twenty operators are far easier than the first twenty. 100x ($6.4bn) is not possible: Bango earns a share of a share of a subscription and the take rate does not support a top-tier payments multiple.
what_kills_it: THE BALANCE SHEET - gross debt tripled from GBP6.89m (Dec-2024) to GBP21.59m (Dec-2025) against GBP5.31m cash, giving net debt equal to 34% of market cap; a covenant issue or rescue rights issue at these prices is the realistic path to permanent loss and would arrive before any good outcome. Disintermediation - Amazon, Google, Apple or a telco consortium could build the plumbing themselves. The gap between 'selected by' and cash can be a year or more; demand the ARR bridge, not the logo slide.
